items.answer: Order matters — the first number compares to the second; 2 : 3 = 0.67 while 3 : 2 = 1.5.

items.stem: An auto-rickshaw meter charges a fixed ₹30 plus ₹15 per km. (i) Find the fare for 5 km and for 10 km. (ii) Is the fare directly proportional to the distance? Explain. (iii) Which part of the fare is proportional to the distance?
items.markingKey: (ii) 105/5 ≠ 180/10 because of the fixed ₹30; (iii) the distance charge ₹15 × km.

items.stem: If x and y are in inverse proportion, which quantity is constant?
In one line: why are speed and time (for a fixed distance) in inverse proportion?
items.answer: Speed × time = distance, which is constant.
items.markingKey: Speed × time = distance, which is constant.

items.stem: A student says 'more workers means more days to finish.' Correct the statement.
items.answer: More workers, FEWER days: workers × days is constant (inverse proportion).
items.markingKey: More workers, FEWER days: workers × days is constant (inverse proportion).

Tap A fills a tank in 6 h and tap B in 3 h. How long do both together take? (Decide first whether this is an inverse-proportion problem.)
items.answer: It is a rates problem, not simple inverse proportion: in 1 h they fill 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 of the tank → 2 h.

items.answer: e.g. y = 10 − x: y falls as x rises, but xy is not constant.
items.markingKey: Inverse proportion needs xy constant, not just opposite movement.

items.stem: A class trip needs 36 litres of water shared equally. (i) Copy and complete: 4 bottles → ? litres each, 6 bottles → ?, 8 bottles → ?. (ii) What stays constant? (iii) Sketch how litres per bottle changes as the number of bottles grows.
items.answer: (i) 9, 6, 4.5 (ii) bottles × litres = 36 (iii) a decreasing curve that never reaches 0
items.markingKey: Inverse proportion table, constant product, hyperbola-like curve.
